topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Transformation Perspective
lecture_lines: Matrices act as functions moving the entire coordinate plane.
A matrix A transforms a vector v into w.
Think of this as a transformation of the grid.
animations: Fade in the coordinate plane background (#FFFFFF) incorporating the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg].
Flash a vector v (#FFFF00) and transform to w (#00FFFF).
Show the grid lines (#808080) warping together with the vector using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg].

sections.title: The Concept of Function Composition
lecture_lines: Composition means applying one transformation after another.
We apply B first, then A to result C.
We want a single matrix C for AB.
Robotic arm rotates then extends its reach.
This sequence equals a combined transformation matrix.
animations: Show a robotic arm object [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] in its initial state.
Animate the arm [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] rotating (applying transformation B).
Animate the arm [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] extending (applying transformation A).
Show a combined single matrix C label (#FF00FF) appearing.
Flash the robotic arm [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] to show the final result C.

sections.title: Visualizing the Chain Reaction
lecture_lines: Track the basis vectors i and j.
B moves basis vectors to new positions.
A then moves those results again.
Final positions define the columns of matrix C.
This chain is the matrix product AB.
animations: Show unit vectors i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) on a 2D plane using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vectors.svg].
Animate i-hat and j-hat moving to their new positions under transformation B.
Animate the transformed vectors moving again under transformation A.
Highlight the final endpoint positions of i-hat and j-hat with a circle (#FFFF00).
Display the columns of matrix C as the coordinates of these final endpoints using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vectors.svg].

sections.title: Deriving the Rule: Why 'Row by Column'?
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so AB does not equal BA.
It tracks where basis vectors end up after two mappings.
Scaling then flipping differs from flipping then scaling.
animations: Display transformation A applied to a shape [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shape.svg] then B.
Display transformation B applied to the same shape then A.
Show that the final shape [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/shape.svg] positions are different, proving non-commutativity.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication is a geometric shortcut.
Multiply matrices once to capture the full movement.
Compute a single matrix for efficient composite transformations.
animations: Show a stack of matrices shrinking into a single matrix C (#00FFFF).
Scale pulse the final matrix C to emphasize efficiency.
